say.en: FM radio, the microwave oven and the TV remote all use electromagnetic waves. None of them is visible. How are they different? In this lesson: Order the spectrum by wavelength and frequency.
Give sources and uses of radio waves, microwaves and infrared.

body.en: All EM waves travel at $c$ in vacuum and differ only in wavelength and frequency, linked by $c = \nu\lambda$. In order of decreasing wavelength: *radio*, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays. The regions overlap; there are no sharp boundaries.
body.kn: ಎಲ್ಲಾ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ಕಾಂತೀಯ ತರಂಗಗಳು ನಿರ್ವಾತದಲ್ಲಿ c ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ತರಂಗಾಂತರ ಮತ್ತು ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಭಿನ್ನ. c = νλ.

All travel at c, so f equals c/ lambda, and the photon energy is hf. The drawn wave is not to scale.

body.en: *Radio* waves (above about 0.1 m) come from accelerated charges in antennas and carry AM, FM, TV and mobile signals. Microwaves (0.1 m to 1 mm) come from klystrons, magnetrons and Gunn diodes; they are used in radar and microwave ovens, whose frequency matches the resonance of water molecules. Infrared (1 mm to 700 nm) comes from hot bodies and molecules; it is called heat waves and is used in remote controls, night vision and physical therapy.
body.kn: ರೇಡಿಯೋ ತರಂಗಗಳು ಆಂಟೆನಾಗಳಿಂದ ಬರುತ್ತವೆ, ಸಂವಹನಕ್ಕೆ ಬಳಕೆ. ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮ ತರಂಗಗಳು ರಾಡಾರ್ ಮತ್ತು ಮೈಕ್ರೋವೇವ್ ಒಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಳಕೆ. ಅವಗೆಂಪು ಕಿರಣಗಳನ್ನು ಉಷ್ಣ ತರಂಗಗಳು ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ; ರಿಮೋಟ್ ಮತ್ತು ರಾತ್ರಿ ದೃಷ್ಟಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಳಕೆ.

lambda equals c over nu equals 3 times 10 to the power 8 / (100 times 10 to the power 6).
lambda equals 3 metres.

lambda is approximately 0.122 metres equals 12.2 centimetres.
So the answer is is approximately 12.2 centimetres.
